title: API Gateway: expired access token
text: Authentication runbook. HTTP 401 with invalid_token or token expired indicates that the gateway rejected the supplied access token. Check the token expiry time, issuer, audience and gateway clock before concluding a cause. An expired access token must be replaced through the approved identity-provider flow. Never paste tokens into a ticket. Check a read-only health endpoint after refreshing credentials. Do not disable authentication or bypass gateway policy. Escalate to the identity team when valid tokens are still rejected.

title: Partner API: rate limiting and backoff
text: Rate limit runbook. HTTP 429 means that the upstream service is rate limiting requests. Inspect Retry-After and the agreed client quota. Respect Retry-After before retrying. Use bounded exponential backoff with jitter and reduce concurrency after operator approval. Do not blindly replay non-idempotent payments or orders. Verify idempotency keys and downstream transaction status before proposing replay. A successful retry does not prove the quota issue has been permanently resolved.

title: Downstream timeout investigation
text: Timeout runbook. HTTP 504 indicates a gateway timeout while waiting for an upstream response. A read timeout is a symptom, not proof that the downstream service is offline. Correlate gateway and upstream timestamps using the correlation ID. Check downstream latency, connection establishment, DNS and queue depth. Do not simply increase timeouts without investigating saturation. Any timeout or concurrency configuration change needs operator approval. Escalate when upstream telemetry is unavailable.

title: JDBC connection pool exhaustion
text: Connection pool runbook. Connection pool exhausted or SQLTransientConnectionException indicates that a database connection could not be acquired within the configured time. Inspect active connections, maximum pool size, slow queries and unclosed connections. Pool exhaustion can be caused by slow queries, leaks or traffic growth; the log alone does not prove which. Capture pool metrics and query latency before proposing a change. Restarting a service or increasing the pool size requires operator approval and a database capacity check.
